answers.answer: Rule is determined by comparing each player's warriors plus buildings in a clearing; tokens and pawns do not count. The player with more than each other player rules it. An ordinary tie means nobody rules. Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle: ‘warriors plus buildings’; ‘Tokens and pawns do not contribute.’

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of your warriors or pawns from a clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. Pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple times in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.

Battle requires your warriors or pawn and an enemy in the chosen clearing; rule is not required. The defender may play a matching-suit ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush, in which case no hits are dealt. Otherwise the ambush causes two immediate hits, not limited by defending warriors; battle ends if the attacker then has no warriors/pawns. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have them), roll: high die is attacker's hits and low die defender's, equal dice give equal results; each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle, Alliance reverses dice, and Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Resolve after-roll effects, then add extra hits (uncapped) and subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker adds one defenseless hit (Vagabond is defenseless only without undamaged swords). For each side's hits, that side chooses its own pieces to remove, but all warriors must go before buildings/tokens; it also orders effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits, and warrior losses do not change the rolled cap retroactively. Removing an enemy building/token scores one VP for the remover, whether attacker or defender and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.

Craft by activating crafting pieces matching the card's bottom-left crafting icons; card suit is not the cost, and each icon needs one activation. Each crafting piece normally activates once per turn; Vagabond can reactivate its pawn for each icon by exhausting a separate face-up, undamaged hammer. An item card cannot be crafted if its item is absent from map supply. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.

During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.

A dominance card spent for suit goes to the available area near the map whenever it would otherwise enter discard. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so the payment must be a bird card; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance card.

For two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal three cards to each player. Cover four R building slots with ruins. The map supply is two boots, two bags, one crossbow, one hammer, two swords, two tea, and two coins; only if Vagabond is in play, its four R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword are hidden one under each ruin. Without Vagabond, ruins have no items. Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is distinct from turn order.

Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply, including removals outside battle. Hospitals have no destination if the Keep is gone. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.

Marquise Daylight first crafts with workshops, then takes up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit. March is one compound action of up to two moves, and you cannot interrupt it to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and may be taken only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot. Take the leftmost building of the chosen type. Pay the column cost by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the uncovered track space. You cannot build without the full wood cost, building, and legal slot.

In Birdsong, first Emergency Orders: if hand is empty draw one. Then add one or two hand cards to Decree, no more than one bird card, placing each in any column; columns have no size limit. Then, if no roost is on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all these pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card column by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column, card order is free and bird is wild. Recruit and Build must occur in a clearing matching that card; Move must move at least one warrior from a matching clearing under ordinary movement requirements; Battle must start in a matching clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build requires a matching clearing you rule, an open slot, and no roost already there. If a required action cannot be fully completed, immediately Turmoil; do not skip it or continue other columns.

Turmoil costs one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Map warriors and buildings remain. End Daylight, then take the normal Evening: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, and discard to five.
answers.evidence: Eyrie > Turmoil, in order; Turmoil does not remove map pieces.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card, birds included, to Supporters per affected move (not per warrior). If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance and Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming card; the payment or no-match draw still happens.

All Revolts must be completed before any Spread Sympathy, with each action repeatable; after spreading begins, no returning to Revolt that Birdsong. Both spend supporters matching the target clearing, with birds wild. Revolt targets a sympathetic clearing with no base and matching a base still on the board; it costs two supporters, removes all enemy pieces, scores one VP per enemy building/token removed, places the matching base, warriors equal to matching-suit sympathetic clearings (including this one), and one officer. Enemy Vagabond instead takes three item damage. Spread Sympathy targets an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy (or any clearing if none exists), costs the amount shown above the next sympathy track token plus one matching supporter under Martial Law if the chosen clearing has at least three warriors of one other player; place sympathy and score its uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing, and Keep placement ban applies.
answers.evidence: Alliance > Birdsong > Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: Train in Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. In Evening, Organize removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there, and scores the uncovered VP; no supporters, adjacency, or Martial Law cost is stated, though legal token placement is needed. Evening operations are limited by officer count, and officers stay on board. Losing a base discards supporters matching its clearing including birds and removes half of officers rounded up; if no bases remain, reduce supporters to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance > Losing a base; Daylight; Evening.

answers.answer: Birdsong Refresh counts tea already face up on Refresh track, flips two exhausted items per such tea, then three more; newly refreshed tea adds nothing during this step. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing; forest adjacency follows map rules, including Winter river. In Daylight, normal Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can go only to adjacent clearing. Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.

Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; taking the last item removes the ruin and frees the slot. Quest is available only in a matching clearing: exhaust its two listed items, complete it, then choose VP equal to completed matching quests including this one, or draw two cards; draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel preserving its face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.

A faction becomes Hostile immediately when Vagabond removes one of its warriors while it is non-Hostile, except the special allied-warrior battle-loss timing. On Vagabond's own turn, battle removal of hostile pieces earns one extra VP per hostile piece, except the warrior that first caused Hostile; no Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile marker out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike removes one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Strike; Hostile; Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile.

answers.answer: Vagabond coalition is available with four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, by activating dominance with a player not already in coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; choose among tied lowest players. Place your score marker on that player's faction board and stop scoring. If the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including by dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not grant Allied powers.

Cards override the Law; the Law overrides Learning to Play. Apply general and faction rules together when possible, with faction rules taking precedence if incompatible. ‘Cannot’ is absolute unless explicitly overridden; an ordinary card does not override it absent an explicit override.

If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses; in battle, the attacker orders effects at the same timing. A March's two moves are one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.

‘At start’ effects happen before all other effects in that phase; ‘at end’ effects happen after everything else in that phase, before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

Hand size is public but hand contents are private; reveal/show only if instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected; the deck cannot. Non-binding agreements do not transfer cards except as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Cards/hand information.

answers.answer: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. When instructed to give or discard non-bird cards, birds must be treated as that suit; a non-bird cannot substitute if the instruction explicitly requires a bird.

Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If instructed to place more pieces than can be placed, place the maximum possible; you cannot voluntarily place fewer. Shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, and does not waive the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.
answers.evidence: Actions > pieces finite/maximum possible; Eyrie Decree.

answers.answer: Pieces placed normally come from supply or, for tracked pieces, the leftmost track space. Removed faction pieces normally return to supply or, for tracked pieces, the rightmost empty track space. Removed items are removed permanently. With simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answers.evidence: Actions > Removed faction pieces; Special Rules > Place/remove/replace.

answers.answer: A forced action is resolved as if the affected player chose it, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

An enemy cannot replace a piece in the Keep clearing because replacement requires legal removal and placement, and only Marquise may place pieces there. A swap ignores move and place restrictions; it is distinct from moving or placing.
If multiple players reach 30 simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player in the comparison.

A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and forests separated by just one printed path; on Winter, the river also divides forests. Slip uses this forest adjacency. Fall has no special rules.
answers.evidence: Shared movement section > forest; Overview says Fall has no special rules; Vagabond Slip.

answers.answer: Marquise supplies 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner; put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop, and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Fill the roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

Alliance supplies 10 warriors, puts three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track, then draws three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from its three-card hand. It starts with no map pieces or officers.

Choose Thief, Tinker, or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins, and bags go face up on matching tracks; other items go face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box. Set each other faction's relationship marker to Indifferent.

Recommended minimum Reach totals are 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base faction values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law permits any mix totaling at least 17 for adventurous groups.

In Birdsong, place one wood per sawmill, limited by the shared supply of eight wood. In Daylight, each Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there, using the same finite supply. In Evening, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
Recruit places the maximum available warriors among eligible recruiters if supply cannot fill all of them; Marquise chooses among eligible recruiters.
Eyrie-crafted items score one VP instead of printed VP under Disdain for Trade. Builder ignores Disdain, so it scores printed item VP. Other extra crafting-point effects still apply under Disdain.
answers.evidence: Eyrie > Disdain for Trade; Builder ability.

answers.answer: Builder: Viziers in Recruit and Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit places two warriors instead of one. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, scores one extra VP in addition to normal removal points.
No. Charismatic Recruit requires placing two warriors, and if the required action cannot be fully completed, the Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil; placing only one does not fulfill it.
answers.evidence: Eyrie > Charismatic ability; Decree requires full completion, including supply limitations.

answers.answer: Guerrilla War does not bypass warrior caps. When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and attacker the lower; warrior caps still apply.
Alliance may inspect Supporters, but they are spent only for suit and cannot be used to craft. They are separate from hand cards and do not count toward the five-card hand limit.

No. All Revolts must occur before starting Spread Sympathy, and once spreading starts the Alliance cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong. Newly spread sympathy therefore cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.
No. Martial Law requires at least three warriors of one other player in the target clearing; two enemy players with two each do not meet that condition. Organize has no Martial Law cost.

Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage, and moving only the Vagabond pawn there does not trigger it. However, if allied warriors accompany the Vagabond and move into sympathy, moving those warriors triggers Outrage; the mover adds one matching card per affected move, not per warrior.

Alliance takes up to its number of officers in Evening operations, in any order and repetition; operations do not consume officers. After operations it draws one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discards down to five. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.
The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead the Vagabond damages three items.

Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum as attacker or defender equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. As defender Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. When taking hits, damage one undamaged item per hit; ignore excess hits if none remain. (Vagabond's battle initiation separately requires exhausting one sword.)

Face-up tea, coins, and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on a track sends it to Satchel. Repair preserves the item's face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space. Damaged items cannot pay actions, even if face up.

Capacity is six items plus two per face-up bag on its track. Count Satchel plus Damaged box; items on tracks do not count. Check capacity as the last Evening step, not immediately on acquisition. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within capacity.

No. Forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh is the Birdsong procedure for flipping exhausted items; Repair exhausts a hammer to move a damaged item to Satchel while keeping its current face.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Birdsong Refresh; Evening Rest; Repair.

answers.answer: Aid exhausts any one item and gives a card matching the Vagabond's clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. No crafted item is required to perform Aid; the Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items if available. To improve a non-Hostile relationship, Aid that faction the number of times printed between current and next spaces in the same turn; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP.

At Allied status, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. The Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany its move, subject to those warriors' own movement restrictions and rule; moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At battle start as attacker, the Vagabond may use warriors of one Allied faction as its own, including against a different enemy, but cannot use that faction's warriors to attack the ally itself.

If the Vagabond uses allied warriors as its own in battle, it may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. At battle end, that ally becomes Hostile if more allied warriors were removed than items damaged in that battle; equal numbers do not trigger Hostility.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Taking hits with an ally.

answers.answer: No: one clearing cannot satisfy mixed fox and rabbit crafting icons, since the clearing must match all icons. The Vagabond can reactivate its pawn for multiple crafting icons, paying one face-up, undamaged hammer per icon. A crafted item can immediately be taken face up into Satchel or track, if the item is in supply.

Thief starts with boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the Vagabond's clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing, with bird always qualifying. Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items, keeping their faces, and immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.
Taking the last hidden item removes the ruin and frees its building slot. Ordinary building placement does not remove a ruin; ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Explore; shared movement section says ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed.

answers.answer: Coalition partners are not enemies, so they cannot be attacked as enemies under the ordinary battle requirement. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition: partners are not enemies; does not grant Allied powers.

answers.answer: Total is 3 VP. Removing the first warrior makes the faction Hostile and that warrior is excluded from Infamy. The second hostile warrior earns one Infamy VP. Removing the hostile building earns one normal removal VP plus one Infamy VP. The normal warrior removals themselves do not score removal VP.

A normal move costs one exhausted boot, plus one extra boot if the destination contains any warriors of any Hostile faction. Hostile buildings alone do not trigger the extra boot. Hostile warriors from multiple factions still trigger only the one stated extra boot.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight > Move; Hostile status movement rule.

answers.answer: No. Taking an available dominance card puts it into hand; activation is a separate act. Neither taking nor activating uses a faction action allowance, including Marquise's.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions > Dominance: taking and activation are separate and neither requires faction action allowance.

answers.answer: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

An immediate-effect crafting card resolves its paper-box effect and is discarded. A persistent-effect card is kept in the play area and its stone-box text applies; it is outside the hand and cannot be spent, discarded, or used for another purpose unless instructed. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in play.

Ambush cards cannot be crafted; a defender may play a matching ambush for two immediate hits, or an attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush. Dominance cards cannot be crafted; activate one to change the victory condition or spend it for suit.
answers.evidence: Actions > Craft (4.1), Ambush and Dominance cards.

answers.answer: Choose factions, then randomly determine starting player and seating. Take faction boards and pieces; choose Fall or Winter. Put score markers at zero; put the battle dice nearby. Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond, and does not determine turn order.
The first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; no need to finish the action, phase, or turn first.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions > 30 VP: ‘wins immediately, on any player's turn.’

answers.answer: To initiate battle, choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy to be defender. You do not need to rule that clearing.

For simultaneous before-roll or after-roll battle effects, the attacker chooses their order if both players have effects. Each side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by removal of its own pieces.
answers.evidence: Actions > Battle (4.3), before/after-roll and deal-hits steps.

answers.answer: In Count Hits, add extra hits, which are uncapped by warriors, then subtract ignored hits.

A non-Vagabond crafting faction takes a crafted item card from the map item supply into its Crafted Items box and scores the printed VP, except Eyrie scores one VP under Disdain for Trade (with Builder ignoring Disdain). Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items to use them as Vagabond does.
Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy. A crafting piece's suit is the suit of its clearing. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.
Mobilize adds a hand card to Supporters, respecting the Supporter cap. Alliance may craft, Mobilize, and Train in any order and number during Daylight; it need not finish crafting first.
In ordinary Evening, score the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, then draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discard to five. This full normal Evening also happens after Turmoil.

Vagabond exhausts one sword to initiate its Daylight Battle action. An exhausted sword cannot pay, because action costs require a face-up, undamaged item; being counted toward rolled hits does not make it ready to exhaust again.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Pawn and items; Daylight > Battle.

answers.answer: A turn proceeds Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. After Evening, play passes clockwise to the next player.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: turns clockwise; Birdsong → Daylight → Evening.

answers.answer: Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice, moving it to the Damaged box without changing its face. Already damaged items cannot absorb another hit; if no undamaged items remain, ignore excess hits.
Alliance may take up to one Evening military operation per officer; officers are not consumed. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.
answers.evidence: Alliance > Evening and military operation table.

answers.answer: The Vagabond has no fixed action count stated; in Daylight it may take the listed item actions in any order and number, as ready undamaged items permit. The same type can be repeated while its costs and other requirements are met.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight: ‘Any order/number, as ready undamaged items permit.’

answers.answer: Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing. The crossbow must be face up and undamaged to pay; an exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight > Strike; Pawn and items.
